record.context_brief: relaxation gap for r=1 vertex cover
record.original_question: For a combinatorial graph G, let β(G) be the size of a minimum vertex cover in G, and let β_1(Γ(G)) be the minimum number of radius-1 balls needed to cover the continuous graph Γ(G) obtained by replacing each edge of G by a unit-length interval. The paper asks for the largest possible value of the relaxation-gap ratio β(G) / β_1(Γ(G)) over all graphs G, with the conjecture that this ratio is at most 2.

evidence.quote: Similarly to the independent set problem above, the following natural open question arises: What is the highest ratio between β(G) and β1(Γ(G)) over all G? Following intuition from the matching theory and known results for the minimum vertex cover problem, we conjecture the ratio is at most 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. The continuous graph Γ(G) associated with G is the metric space obtained by replacing each edge e∈E with a unit-length closed interval, identifying intervals at common endpoints, and equipping the resulting topological space with the path metric in which every edge has length 1. Points of Γ(G) thus include the vertices of G together with all interior points of the edges, and the distance between two points x,y∈Γ(G) is the length of a shortest path in Γ(G) connecting them. For a point x∈Γ(G), let B_1(x)={y∈Γ(G): d(x,y)≤1} denote the closed ball of radius 1 centered at x.

Define:
• β(G) = the minimum size of a vertex cover of G, i.e. the smallest cardinality of a set S⊆V such that every edge of G has at least one endpoint in S.
• β_1(Γ(G)) = the minimum number of radius-1 closed balls (with centers chosen anywhere in Γ(G)) whose union is all of Γ(G).

Determine
   sup_G  β(G) / β_1(Γ(G)),
where the supremum is taken over all finite simple graphs G with at least one edge. In particular, decide whether this supremum is at most 2.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question with a conjectured upper bound of 2 in a recent survey on combinatorial properties of continuous graphs. Web searches did not surface any resolution of the conjecture; standard literature on vertex cover integrality gaps and ball packing/covering in graphs does not directly address this specific ratio.

status_evidence.title: Packing and Covering Balls in Graphs Excluding a Minor
status_evidence.snippet: Studies vertex sets meeting all balls of a given radius in minor-closed graph classes; does not resolve the β(G)/β_1(Γ(G)) ratio for continuous graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related ball-covering literature does not address the specific continuous-graph ratio.
